description: Coverage accounting. 'quarantine' lists tests that no CI leg executes, each with an owner, a review date and the gap it leaves; the Safety evidence job fails on any other never-executed test. 'dispositions' explain removed or weakened coverage; check_coverage_regression.py accepts only dispositions added by the same change. See docs/rules/safety-evidence.md.

quarantine.reason: Collation.Default snapshots the culture once per process, so the test passes only as the first LiteDB use in the process; after another test created a database it sees that culture instead of 'fi'.
quarantine.gap: A new database taking its collation from the current thread culture is not asserted on any CI leg; product behaviour (process-wide snapshot) decides whether the test can be made order-independent.

quarantine.reason: Not supported yet: rebuilding 'ana'/'ANA' from en-US/None to en-US/IgnoreCase throws 'Cannot insert duplicate key' instead of recording the collision in _rebuild_errors.
quarantine.gap: Rebuilding to a collation under which unique keys collide is not exercised; the expected _rebuild_errors behaviour is not implemented.

quarantine.reason: Takes ~102 s (100 iterations with a 1 s sleep; passed 5/5 locally on net10.0). The DiskWriterQueue race of #2127 no longer exists; the queue was removed in 198f0a672.
quarantine.gap: Back-to-back file-backed inserts into 100 recreated databases do not run in CI; the original race cannot recur, so the test is a candidate to retire as obsolete.

dispositions.invariant: Transaction retry must release obsolete Shared writer ownership, preserve active transaction guards, and allow other threads and processes to progress after completion.
dispositions.reason: Repair the stale permanentGuard reference left by d4713d40bf382baf87c3f18498e85feb5bc33fb7. P3-FX F2 renamed and strengthened the failed-registration test to require immediate release after implicit abort, rather than retain an already-ended transaction's hold. The existing p3fx-aborted-retry-releases-legacy-ownership disposition records that behavior correction; retry, rollback, peer progress and cold data/index/sentinel assertions remain. No test or known-bad proof pin changes here.

dispositions.invariant: Production performance evidence is CI-only, uses isolated before/after libraries, keeps durability modes and runtimes separate and verifies the resulting database independently; the ordinary benchmark gate remains exhaustive.
dispositions.reason: Add a separately selected, fork-only Linux x64 job with a finite 20-minute job/15-minute process budget and error on missing evidence. Existing comparison, preattached tenure and open/close jobs remain available. The new input excludes the unrelated comparison job only when explicitly requested. Identical candidate timing programs measure fresh process attachments against df6b16f80 and the fixed candidate, with positive CHECKPOINT, real writer admission, raw p50/p99 samples and cold row/index/sentinel checks. Fake-worker unit tests validate ordering without running measurements locally.

dispositions.invariant: A failed retry Begin must not create an extra native hold, discard a still-active transaction, or prevent another thread from making progress after completion.
dispositions.reason: Renamed and strengthened the existing encrypted/plain, pinned/unpinned retry test for the corrected implicit-abort lifetime. It now requires zero obsolete transaction holds immediately after abort and after failed registration, installs the same registration fault on the reopened core, and retains successful retry, rollback, foreign-thread progress and exact cold data/index/sentinel checks. The old expectation of one hold after an already-ended inner transaction is the confirmed stale-ownership defect, not a supported active-transaction invariant.

dispositions.invariant: The removed tests required the experimental opt-in to round-trip and replace immediate same-thread foreign-facade refusal with a TIMEOUT-bounded wait.
dispositions.reason: The owner removed the opt-in for Phase 3: legacy same-thread foreign-facade writes always throw SAME_THREAD_TRANSACTION (141). Cooperative waiting is deferred to Phase 4 thread-independent transaction handles. The retained Direct, legacy Shared and mapped Shared tests require immediate code-141 refusal, successful owner rollback and separate-thread progress after commit; the removed setting and its obsolete waiting behavior must not be restored.

dispositions.invariant: Every discovered Shared test executes exactly once per leg with the runtime/hook guards, unchanged assertions, concurrency and 300-second session limit; a stalled test cannot count as complete.
dispositions.reason: Retained 40521868246 TRX files show ongoing serial completions until all four Linux shared session aborts; passing x64 net9/net10 need 258.7/268.9 seconds of test work. Split maintenance-crash, final-close, rebuild and tenure from the shared complement; preserve process partitions and exhaustive discovery accounting. Add 120-second per-test blame-hang mini dumps and sequence artifacts, retaining failure status. No tests or fault cuts are removed and no timeout is raised.

dispositions.invariant: Three simultaneously accepted reader generations retain exact indexed payloads and unrelated data through checkpoint; the protected slow path remains explicitly exercised.
dispositions.reason: Replace the obsolete slice-4 assertion that warm reads do not exist with two executed theory cases. An identity ReadTransform keeps the original zero-warm-hit slow path; the default case preserves all exact generation/index/sentinel/file assertions and additionally proves real warm hits with the final generation. Adds one discovered case; neither case is skipped.

dispositions.invariant: Real ownership handoff, retired-core generation isolation, late-read disposal, retry hold balance, unchanged degraded-sync fences and the single authority-file contract remain exercised.
dispositions.reason: Mapped Phase 3 uses pins without anchor readers and retains cores after commit/rollback. Capture the actual pin after Begin; demand and await native release before asserting it is free or a core is retired; use the mapped holder teardown cut for dead-owner cleanup; probe WRITE exclusion before the degraded-sync handoff; resolve the WAL filename with FileHelper. Preserve all exact cold data, authority, fence and foreign-callback assertions and add actual-generation/retirement controls.

dispositions.invariant: Writer-end death tests must reach and pause the actual mapped close publication before the child returns a completion marker or exits. Existing cold and snapshot recovery oracles are unchanged.
dispositions.reason: Capture the retained pin under an explicit transaction and demand its actual release at writer-end. Ordinary auto-commit now returns before retained close, so the old harness could print committed or exit before the death cut. Added metadata/WAL-reset/close-cut commands preserve existing modes; encrypted logical WAL-zero validation accounts for its physical encryption header.

dispositions.invariant: A releasing holder must not borrow an outstanding local request ticket or barge past the older remote requester; all twelve real handoffs and exact cold state remain checked.
dispositions.reason: The original R1 synchronous loop required unfair reacquisitions to complete before releasing the paused older requests, which deadlocks a correct FIFO fix. The unchanged review commits were merged first. The loop now runs on a separate actual Thread, proves it queues without admission, releases both older callers, asserts every reacquisition ticket exceeds the remote ticket, and joins all workers before retaining the original twelve-handoff and cold exact oracles.

dispositions.invariant: Existing full CI and benchmark comparisons remain unchanged by default; Phase 3-A measurements run only on the fork in isolated production builds.
dispositions.reason: Adds an opt-in Linux net8/net10 job comparing exact Phase 2 against the candidate, five alternating paired rounds, durable and nonsync small transactions and two-process alternating latency. A bounded job and required artifacts add evidence without reducing existing thresholds or tests.

dispositions.invariant: Implicit abort immediately returns transaction ownership; retry registration faults must target the actual retry core and reader cleanup must use actual Thread identity. All five adversarial scenarios and all assertions remain. R3 probes WRITE after joining the awakened peer, since probing earlier races legitimate successor ownership.
dispositions.reason: R1 previously dereferenced the facade current core after abort, which the required immediate native teardown now closes/clears. Capture that exact core before the duplicate and assert its abort afterwards. A deterministic sibling holds the awakened peer in its transaction and proves the old unconditional free-WRITE oracle is invalid; the retained R3 scenario now joins the peer before its raw probe. Retry injection now targets a retained pin core or the newly opened ordinary core. Lifetime reflection follows Dictionary<Thread,int>. No test is removed, skipped or weakened.

dispositions.invariant: Existing production benchmark gate scenarios and thresholds remain required by their original triggers; mapped startup evidence must identify both exact production libraries and verify retained data.
dispositions.reason: Adds an explicit fork-only manual mode for baseline a878a10c6 versus the selected candidate, net8/net10 on Linux x64, five alternating pairs of 50 open/close cycles. Existing comparison selection is unchanged unless this new mode is explicitly requested; no safety test, matrix, timeout or threshold is removed or lowered.

dispositions.invariant: Preserve complete acknowledged payloads, exact secondary-index results, unrelated data and byte-preserving read-only recovery; interrupted transactions expose only complete protocol-permitted outcomes, including a second interrupted checksum recovery.
dispositions.reason: WalPadding.Pad skips equal-length SetLength, removing modeled before/after-truncate events and changing the number of recorded PRNG words. These stream-backed targets never use the combined FileStream write. Re-pin both input and trace hashes at unchanged seeds/counts after all target oracles completed; retain every old hash in previousHashes and the unchanged deterministic recovery guards. No oracle, expected-failure classification or actual persistent transition is removed.

dispositions.reason: WalPadding.Pad skips equal-length SetLength, removing modeled before/after-truncate events and changing the number of recorded PRNG words. dispositions.invariant: Preserve complete acknowledged payloads, exact secondary-index results, unrelated data and byte-preserving read-only recovery; compact interruption exposes only whole original/new transactions with stable membership through checkpoint.
dispositions.reason: WalPadding.Pad skips equal-length SetLength, removing modeled before/after-truncate events and changing the number of recorded PRNG words. These stream-backed targets never use the combined FileStream write. Re-pin both input and trace hashes at unchanged seeds/counts after all target oracles completed; retain every old hash in previousHashes and the unchanged deterministic recovery guards. No oracle, expected-failure classification or actual persistent transition is removed.

dispositions.invariant: Released engines must refuse newer WAL-bearing files without changing data or WAL bytes; the current engine must recover every acknowledged document across padding alignment boundaries.
dispositions.reason: Prepends padding-create, released LiteDB 5.0.21 padding refusal, and padding-verify to the existing compatibility chain. Adds eight fixtures (plain/encrypted at 1, 127, 128 and 129 acknowledged commits); retains every existing compatibility invocation and assertion.

dispositions.invariant: Released engines must refuse newer WAL-bearing files without changing data or WAL bytes; the current engine must recover every acknowledged document across padding alignment boundaries.
dispositions.reason: Adds padding-create and padding-verify dispatch to WalPaddingCompatibility. Captures aligned WAL-bearing plain/encrypted files before writer disposal at 1, 127, 128 and 129 commits, then checks every document payload through two recovery/checkpoint opens after legacy refusal. Existing dispatcher paths remain intact.

dispositions.invariant: Released engines must refuse newer WAL-bearing files without changing data or WAL bytes; the current engine must recover every acknowledged document across padding alignment boundaries.
dispositions.reason: Adds padding dispatch for eight plain/encrypted WAL fixtures at 1, 127, 128 and 129 acknowledged commits. Reuses the existing Refuse oracle against actual LiteDB 5.0.21 for read, write, rebuild and upgrade; each refusal checks byte-identical data and WAL. Existing reclaim and other modes retain their checks.

dispositions.invariant: Benchmark verdicts require complete measurement sets, unchanged owner thresholds and independently verified candidate identities; partial or subset measurements cannot pass the Phase 1 gate.
dispositions.reason: Optional baseline_ref adds same-job v5/before/after evidence with a 23-minute measurement budget and 29-minute job limit. Default jobs retain their existing rounds, timeouts, workloads and verdicts. Incomplete comparisons fail evidence validation; explicit scenario subsets are report-only. Synthetic comparison tests verify shared-v5 identity, separate before/after binaries, rotating order, bounds and subset verdict refusal. No product tests or safety assertions are removed.

dispositions.invariant: Complete alternating A/B round sets and unchanged owner thresholds are required before judging performance; ambiguous high-spread measurements cannot pass.
dispositions.reason: macOS increases from six to ten rounds with a 24-minute measurement budget and 29-minute job limit (the original hosted macOS jobs took 6–7 minutes). Partial sets still fail validation; Linux/Windows retain six rounds and their existing job limits. The old unconditional-noise expectation is replaced with clear range-bound pass/fail, ambiguous noise, threshold-boundary and fivefold-regression tests. No product tests, safety assertions or fault coverage change.

dispositions.invariant: Every discovered test method belongs to exactly one complete-suite partition; every session retains the 300-second limit and runtime/architecture and test-hook guards.
dispositions.reason: Split engine shared coordination and allocation families and shared mapped/upgrade process families into separate sessions using Windows TRX timing evidence. No tests, assertions, concurrency or failure injection are removed; the unchanged discovery verifier and per-leg evidence manifest account for every partition.

dispositions.invariant: Every test leg's results are uploaded and judged; no existing timeout, filter or partition changes.
dispositions.reason: Adds the Safety policy and Safety evidence jobs (10-minute limits) and a results upload for the .NET Framework leg, which uploaded nothing before; existing test steps keep their timeouts and filters.

dispositions.invariant: Every .NET Framework test remains in the complete xunit.console assembly run and has enough job time to finish and upload its evidence.
dispositions.reason: Retain the unfiltered net462/net481 assembly while raising the Windows Framework job limit from 20 to 35 minutes. Recent net481 evidence took 1,079 seconds and the current run reached 1,215 seconds before cancellation; 35 minutes leaves at least 42.1% headroom at that observed point. No test, filter, assertion or evidence partition is removed.

dispositions.invariant: LiteDatabase(Stream) checkpoints each commit into the caller's stream and leaves the persisted checkpoint pragma as it was.
dispositions.reason: The stream constructor no longer persists CHECKPOINT=1 at all (a 5.0.21 regression fixed in this PR), so the test asserts the pragma never changes, that a commit reaches the stream, and that it is still 1000 after disposal.

dispositions.invariant: Every smoke leg still runs its targets with unchanged seeds, counts, timeouts and artifact uploads.
dispositions.reason: Adds an upload of each smoke leg's markers.json files (warn when none) and a 10-minute Reachability gate job that judges them after all legs; no existing step, timeout or filter changes.

dispositions.invariant: Every existing build and test leg keeps its steps, filters, timeouts and evidence; the Safety evidence job still requires all of them.
dispositions.reason: Adds the always-run Oracle smoke job (15-minute limit; oracle self-tests selected by a filter, the oracle-wired fuzz targets at count 10, reachability report, evidence upload that must not be empty), makes Safety evidence depend on it and declares it for the pr and full tiers; the Safety policy job also runs the reachability registry check.

dispositions.invariant: Every index-migration recovery case runs to completion and checks its oracle.
dispositions.reason: The harness now reports how far a case got when it times out (write count, WAL pages, commit state and elapsed time on stderr), for diagnosis, and the per-command timeout that guards against hangs is 300 s instead of 90 s because slow Windows runners took 86 s for one stage; no case or oracle changed.

dispositions.invariant: Every existing test leg keeps its timeout, filter and partition; the released v4/v5 corpus is checked on every PR.
dispositions.reason: Adds the released-file-compatibility job (20-minute limit): Linux/ICU and Windows/NLS on PR runs, plus Windows/ICU and macOS/ICU on full runs. The Safety evidence job requires it. Existing jobs are unchanged. Fixtures listed in tools/ReleaseCompatibility/pending-activation.json are run and must still fail with their recorded diagnostic.

dispositions.invariant: Never expose bytes beyond FileStorage metadata length; detect a loaded chunk that overruns it.
dispositions.reason: The previous guard accepted a truncated successful read of corrupt chunks. The replacement requires a corruption error even when the caller requests exactly the declared length, with sequential and seek controls.

dispositions.invariant: Legacy caller-stream regressions use authenticated damaged-document and dropped-index fixture bytes without changing the release corpus.
dispositions.reason: Unions the S07 fixture inventory with the S01 empty manifest now on dev. Adds two archives pinned to e059a85e1cbd641e4a682882a70b1c84906d393f and their unchanged SHA-256 hashes; no existing fixture entry is removed or repinned, and the release corpus has its separate manifest.

dispositions.invariant: Released dropped-index and prerelease vector fixtures remain pinned and hash-verified alongside the S01 corpus scaffold.
dispositions.reason: S01 has an empty fixture map at revision 88b857f6; preserve the two S05 entries and their unchanged hashes at e059a85e1cbd641e4a682882a70b1c84906d393f. No fixture is removed or repinned.

dispositions.invariant: The pinned corpus producer must match its exact recorded source hash; all 56 fixture/archive/database hashes and pending-failure diagnostics remain enforced.
dispositions.reason: Preserves the byte-identical original generator in tools/ReleaseCompatibility/provenance/generate-release-corpus.py while the current operational tool gains bounded timeouts. The verifier still requires an exact producer hash match and rejects unknown producer hashes.

dispositions.invariant: Explicit transactions that only read must commit or roll back without modifying caller data, including a partial page tail; write APIs must not acknowledge volatile-only changes.
dispositions.reason: Changes the existing no-match DeleteMany assertion from successful no-op to IOException when no caller log is supplied, matching the intentional refusal of all write operations before acknowledgement. Retains indexed reads, byte preservation, commit and rollback assertions and executes them for both partial-tail cases; adds eight loss/refusal regressions and two caller-file-log retention controls. No test is removed or skipped.

dispositions.invariant: A queued writer must be refused when a failed seek leaves the WAL uncertain; a safely removed unconfirmed append may permit continued use, as documented in the PR summary and WAL failure-containment release notes.
dispositions.reason: The review-round-2 seek/IOException row incorrectly required terminal stop even after successful append truncation. Replace it with both exception types plus observed failed truncation, retaining every terminal-stop and queued-writer assertion. The expanded safe-seek control covers both original exception types, a queued acknowledged writer, a subsequent commit and two file-backed recovery opens. Existing Disk_Tests retain publication/reservation/length assertions and gain explicit non-stopped and zero-ownership checks.

dispositions.invariant: Legacy WAL, dropped-index and prerelease-vector guards use immutable, hash-verified released fixtures.
dispositions.reason: Current dev contains the two reviewed S05 fixtures from squash-merged #3060. Add the four S06 WAL fixtures while retaining all six entries and unchanged SHA-256 values at e059a85e1cbd641e4a682882a70b1c84906d393f; no fixture bytes or expectations are removed or repinned.

dispositions.invariant: Existing CI tests, filters, timeouts and runtime legs remain intact; pinned legacy WAL files are also checked with the production assembly.
dispositions.reason: Adds the six production compatibility scenarios and the Python harness timeout/cleanup guards to the existing compatibility job. No existing case or oracle changes.

dispositions.invariant: Only qualified Linux x64 may enable ABI-2 mappings. Native range tests remain enabled on all targets; existing default-mode tests are unchanged.
dispositions.reason: The new ABI-2 prototype is dormant and explicitly refuses unqualified mapped platforms. These new tests execute on Linux; Windows/macOS/ARM qualification remains a blocking gap, not a passing claim.

dispositions.invariant: Mapped publication cuts retain process-death evidence and registered reachability.
dispositions.reason: The previous entry omitted a hook family and used a marker label instead of the actual PublicationStage injector. Register the real delegate and literal marker; retain the original test reference and add live-DMS, terminal-stop and prefix evidence. No test is removed or weakened.

dispositions.invariant: Collected cold and warm streams release all generation ownership; remote checkpoints drain the WAL completely and preserve committed data.
dispositions.reason: The parent authorized correcting the original oracle: an absent WAL after successful checkpoint is length zero; a present nonempty WAL still fails. Both original zero-length assertions, all other assertions and the second checkpoint/manual-cleanup sequence remain. Added bounded asynchronous waits (10 seconds with diagnostic failure) for the original deferred-cleanup conditions, without relaxing them. Retained the corrected lifetime sibling because its one-checkpoint sequence is not byte-for-byte identical. No test is removed or skipped.

dispositions.invariant: ABI-2 executes every existing case on qualified little-endian Linux x64 and refuses all other runtime/platform targets without mutating storage. Native range-lock tests stay enabled everywhere.
dispositions.reason: The existing one-file attributes now use the same product predicate, including endianness; no previously qualified target is removed. An ordinary Fact checks the predicate independently, positively opens twice on qualified platforms and asserts repeated physical-file refusal with byte-preserved data/WAL and indexed cold reads on Framework, Windows, macOS and ARM64.

dispositions.invariant: Process-death cuts, mapped reader floors, durability failure hooks and last-close schedules must reach the operation they assert, with identical payload/index/recovery oracles.
dispositions.reason: Hosted /tmp is RAM-backed and is correctly refused by ABI-2. Only ABI-2 fixtures select the existing qualified-volume helper, falling back to the workspace on the same policy as product; no skip is added. General TempFile still uses the same original temporary volume, with canonical spelling so Darwin /var aliases cannot bypass equality-based fault hooks. Direct hooks compare canonical spellings. No assertion, cut, timeout or configured test matrix is removed.

dispositions.invariant: A stopped child remains kernel-live; after child death its DMS, slot and WRITE ownership disappear while the observer remains open.
dispositions.reason: Canonicalize the original temporary path for the alias-refusing range backend; keep every native platform enabled. Declare that shared files remain open during Kill, preventing the Windows cleanup helper from asking for exclusive access against the intentional observer. The actual three-range release assertions are unchanged.

dispositions.invariant: After a failed/retried explicit transaction, an independent child must perform 20 real writes within five seconds while the parent reader survives.
dispositions.reason: Use a new ready/continue handshake to distinguish runtime startup from operation liveness. The harness retains exact parent runtime/architecture guards, its existing 20-second startup bound and the original five-second write bound; no completion, data or lock assertion is relaxed.
